clue.text: Unaware a sailing man told to go was upset

parts.note: an AB, an able seaman, is a sailor
someone told to go is sent away
to have minded something is to have objected or been put out by it

explanation.surface: A sailor who has been dismissed takes it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sailing man' together gives AB, not A plus a separate sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent-minded is distracted and oblivious to what is going on around them.

clue.text: Big noise occupying a large dwelling

indicators.note: a thing occupying a space sits inside it, so the noise goes within the other letters

parts.note: large means big
a din is a loud, big noise

explanation.surface: Something loud fills a sizeable house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' is part of the noise, not a size: a din is a big noise, and 'large' alone gives the size word that 'occupying' opens.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is an old word for to dwell, so abiding and dwelling are participles of synonyms.

clue.text: The school-head is' getting onto a pupil for showing fibre

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of school is S
taken as written; the stray apostrophe is a printing mark
L, for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A headteacher seems to be showing a student some fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting onto' just lines the pieces up in order: S and IS come before A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre made from agave leaves, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Proposes to 'represent Minnesota

indicators.note: read as re-present, to present the letters of the state's name again in a new order

explanation.surface: A politician puts forward candidates to stand for the state of Minnesota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represent' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal: re-present the letters of MINNESOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put their name forward as a candidate.

clue.text: Chief is in deep water

explanation.surface: A leader finds himself out of his depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means principal or chief; the main is a poetic word for the open sea.

clue.text: Dreamy music that's just no go in church

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the go is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Certain music in church is simply not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is a noun here, a turn in a game, not a verb meaning leave; 'in' sets it inside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a soft, dreamy piece of music evoking the night, such as those Chopin wrote for piano.

clue.text: Woman holding gold in a Portuguese city

indicators.note: a person holding something has it inside, so the woman's name wraps the metal

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A woman carrying gold through a city in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Evora is a historic walled city in the Alentejo region of Portugal.

clue.text: If there's many a delay, pretend to be sick

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for a great many
to linger is to delay or dawdle

explanation.surface: Someone facing many hold-ups thinks of feigning illness.
explanation.walkthrough: M for 'many' is a crossword convention from the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to fake or exaggerate illness to dodge work or duty.

clue.text: A heavenly body, awfully remote

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters of remote are jumbled

explanation.surface: A celestial object sits terribly far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a body from space that burns up as a shooting star in the sky.

clue.text: Unlikely to be caught napping!

parts.note: the idiom means alert and watchful, but read literally it describes someone who can hardly ever get to sleep

explanation.surface: A person always on the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepless person is never found dozing, because they cannot drop off.

clue.text: Declaim Beethoven's Sixth to class

indicators.note: the sixth letter of the composer's name is taken, not his symphony

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Lecturing a class about Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Sixth' looks like the Pastoral Symphony but means letter six of BEETHOVEN, which is O.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak pompously or at length, as declaiming does.

clue.text: Domestic kind of revenue

explanation.surface: Home taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland means within a country, so domestic rather than foreign; the Inland Revenue was the UK's tax-collecting body.

clue.text: The parish priest coming round at four will be helpful

indicators.note: the priest's title comes round, enclosing the numeral

parts.note: a curate is a parish clergyman, an assistant to the vicar
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A vicar's assistant who calls in at four o'clock will be welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at four' reads as a time but supplies the Roman IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curative heals, so it is helpful to a sick person.

clue.text: Soldier ants are enormous creatures

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldier ants are huge.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier ants are a real kind of ant, but here 'Soldier' is GI on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Giants are beings of huge size, as in myth and fairy tale.

clue.text: One's held up by a Red Indian grazing

indicators.note: the warrior's word holds the turned piece within it

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, in dated language

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: one is I, and 's adds S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone is robbed by a warrior on the plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' looks like a robbery, but 'up' turns the letters of 'One's' and 'held' puts them inside the warrior, giving SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive means scraping or rubbing away, as a graze scrapes skin.

clue.text: Compromise with intention to cause resentment

parts.note: an end is an aim or intention
anger is resentment or rage

explanation.surface: Settling a dispute in a way designed to cause bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compromise' is a verb here, meaning to put at risk, not a noun for a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety or security is to expose it to danger.

clue.text: The militant malcontent put a point to this car-maker

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: the clue words go to make the answer, read as raw material reworked

explanation.surface: A militant critic attacks a motor manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car-maker' looks like a motor firm, but 'maker' tells you to rework A, N and THIS CAR into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist rejects all government and may agitate or rebel against authority.

clue.text: Bounty ——- great ship, and English built

parts.note: great means large
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Reward for a big, English-built ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity, gifts given freely, so a bounty.

clue.text: Go on, plug the beast!

parts.note: to harp on is to go on about something
to seal is to plug a gap

explanation.surface: Someone urges a friend to keep at it and shoot the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' is to keep going on, HARP on, not encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp seal is an Arctic seal, an animal hunted for its fur.

clue.text: The village wood-turner must wear headgear

indicators.note: a thing worn is surrounded, so the hat goes round the wood

parts.note: a hat is headgear

indicators.note: the wood is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: elm is a wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter in the village has to put on a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wood-turner' looks like a craftsman, but '-turner' turns the tree's name round, giving MLE, and 'must wear' puts it inside the headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village.

clue.text: Darling children were his inspiration

parts.note: the Darling family's children, Wendy, John and Michael, star in Peter Pan, so the clue points to that play's author

explanation.surface: A man inspired by beloved youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment but is the surname of the family in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan, in which the children of the Darling family fly to Neverland.

clue.text: Breathe fast

explanation.surface: Panting.
explanation.definitionFit: To express is to utter, or breathe, words; an express train or letter is a fast one.

clue.text: Guess I am the product of cruel treatment

indicators.note: the answer is produced from the clue words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abused speculates on how they turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Misusage is ill use or abuse, harsh treatment of someone.

clue.text: Fishing net used in river

explanation.surface: Fishermen working on a French waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A seine is a large fishing net hung vertically; the Seine is the river through Paris.

clue.text: Put in charge, step back, keeping a cool head

indicators.note: stepping back, the word for step is read backwards

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: A newly promoted manager stands back and keeps calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping a cool head' sounds like staying calm, but 'cool head' is the definition: polar ice capping the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice on a mountain top or pole, a cold covering at the top.

clue.text: Lines exposing hypocrisy over love

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, pious talk
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: Love poetry that shows up false piety.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a section of a long poem, a group of lines.

clue.text: A knot tier stood up

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a rank is a tier or row

explanation.surface: Someone who ties knots got to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tier' looks like one who ties, but it means a row, RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarled lump in wood or on a tree trunk.

clue.text: The last of the poetry read in a wooden voice

indicators.note: the answer sits in the letters of the two words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A dull reader drones the end of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last of the poetry' looks like the letter Y but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a poem, its final part.

clue.text: Feeling for one in time perhaps

indicators.note: the single letter is placed within the prison term

parts.note: doing time is serving a sentence, so a sentence is an example of time
I is one

explanation.surface: Emotion for a particular moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' is a prison term, a SENTENCE, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive.

clue.text: All the junketing bores a client to distraction

indicators.note: driven to distraction, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Endless partying drives a customer mad with boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Junketing is lavish feasting and partying, and celebrations are festivities.
